result.killer: No single killer. The case is weakened by facts: the re-registration is a one-off that only legacy SEC/HIGC HOAs must do (HLURB-registered HOAs and condo corporations are excluded, and the affected count is unpublished), filing is paper-based at regional offices, and the recurring annual report is a simple GIS plus a CPA-audited FS. I found no annual deadline or penalty I could verify.
result.reason: I found no product, free state portal or association tool that does the core job. Qmunidad and the foreign HOA apps don't cover DHSUD filings, and filing appears to happen on paper at DHSUD regional offices (a third-party listing says triplicate copies and a PHP 1,880 fee). The market is the weak point. DO 2026-007 is a one-off deadline that covers only legacy SEC/HIGC-registered HOAs. HLURB-registered HOAs and condo corporations are excluded, and nobody publishes how many HOAs are affected. About 26,000 HOAs are registered in total, so the affected subset is unknown and probably much smaller. The recurring annual GIS is a simple form, and the audited FS needs a CPA anyway. Volunteer boards have little budget. Annual deadlines and penalties are still unverified.

result.killer: None found. Partial weakeners: AMLC filing through GoTRACS is free; foreign bureau-de-change POS products (CurrencyXchanger, FXPlus, PSTForex) already do the transaction logging, though without BSP or AMLC output; most of the MSB count is probably remittance sub-agents and pawnshops on their principal's systems (my inference, not confirmed).
result.reason: I found nothing that kills it. The duty is current: BSP Circular 1206, approved by Monetary Board Resolution 1362 on 28 Nov 2024, consolidated the money service business rules into the M-Regulations, and the BSP keeps revoking registrations for AML failures. No product built for small Philippine money changers turned up. The tools that exist are enterprise AML (Tookitaki), foreign bureau-de-change POS (CurrencyXchanger, FXPlus, PSTForex, which targets Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia and Thailand) and Mohur's 247 RemitPlus from 2016, with no sign it is still sold. The market is weaker than it looks. Filing through GoTRACS is free. Few small changers will see cash over PHP 500k in a day, so the work is mostly KYC records and STRs. The 7,357 MSB count includes remittance sub-agents, e-money issuers and pawnshops that use their principal's systems. I could not read the text of Circular 1206.

result.reason: The duty is real and still in force. I found no deferral or repeal, and no Supreme Court portal for filing the monthly report: it is still done by email. The candidate is less open than claimed, though. The Stanford TechIndex lists getnotaryo (Cebu, active, subscription; site www.getnotaryo.app). candidates.category: 32. Small fisherfolk and fishing boat operators
candidates.existing: The BFAR FishR/BoatR national database is a state system.
candidates.name: Municipal fisherfolk and boat registration (FishR/BoatR) support for LGU fisheries offices and fisherfolk associations
candidates.trigger: Municipal boats of 3 GT or less must be registered with the LGU (EO 305, Fisheries Code s.19, RA 10654). Annual registration windows are set by LGUs (Loon 6 Jan-23 Apr 2026; Kawit to 26 Feb 2026) and often include boat insurance. Davao City requires fisherfolk licences.
candidates.trigger_note: Probably out of scope (state system, individual buyers). Listed for completeness.
candidates.unchecked: Whether any private operator or association pays; this is largely building the state's registry, which is out of scope.

candidates.category: 33. Micro-business tax and invoicing duties
candidates.existing: Generic bookkeeping and tax tools (Juan(Tax) and others per K14). BIR's own ORUS/eBIRForms are free.
candidates.known_note: Generic micro-business tax filing is excluded by the contract, and the neighbouring ideas K12, K14 and K15 were rejected. The EOPT and e-invoicing changes exempt micro taxpayers, so there is no deadline shock.
candidates.name: Sari-sari / micro-store percentage tax (2551Q) and books-of-accounts filing helper
candidates.trigger: Quarterly 2551Q (about the 25th day after quarter end; unverified against a BIR issuance). Books of accounts registered through ORUS. The PHP 500 annual fee was abolished by EOPT (RA 11976). Micro taxpayers are exempt from the 31 Dec 2026 e-invoicing mandate (RMC 098-2026).

candidates.existing: BSP buying stations and the Cebuana Lhuillier accredited buyer pilot (Paracale, Sagada, 2024). Most miners sell on the black market. No software found.

The BSP reports sales to the BIR monthly. The 3-year transition from 2020 may have been extended (unverified). Only 53 Minahang Bayan were declared as of July 2025.

candidates.trigger: RA 9514 annual FSIC, prerequisite to the Mayor's permit; the sanitary permit; barangay clearance; renewals around January. coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: One search. No national beekeeper or apiary registration or recurring report found. DA AO 14 (2012) put apiculture under BAI (current status unverified). Rules found cover only live-bee imports (BAI importer registration, SPS clearance, CITES), a 2025 organic beekeeping standard (PNS/BAFS 404:2025) and a honey product standard still in draft in mid-2026. No FDA honey rule found. No recurring register or report, so no candidate.

coverage.category: 31. DENR-licensed small operators: chainsaw owners, wood processing plants, tree-cutting/private land timber permits
coverage.found: Chainsaw registration (RA 9175, DAO 2003-24): certificate valid 2 years and renewable (5 years for orchard farmers), though sources conflict on validity. DENR has a web Chainsaw Information System and e-Frontline online chainsaw registration. Lumber dealers file monthly stock purchase and disposition reports by the 5th of the following month via OLDPMS (already covered by the first pass). Wood processing plant permits are decentralised under DAO 2021-05. The monthly or quarterly production report format was not confirmed. Tree-cutting permits moved to regional executive directors under DAO 2021-11, and a Private Land Timber Permit applies on titled land. Duties are mostly one-off or 2-year, so frequency is low. Candidate C1 (weak).

coverage.category: 32. Small fisherfolk and fishing boat operators: BFAR FishR/BoatR, commercial fishing vessel licences, LGU fisheries licences
coverage.found: Municipal boats of 3 GT or less are registered by the LGU (EO 305, Fisheries Code s.19). Registration (FishR/BoatR) is annual, in LGU windows that vary (Loon 6 Jan-23 Apr 2026, Kawit to 26 Feb 2026, Davao City licences). Boat insurance is bundled in some LGUs. Commercial vessels of 3.1 GT or more renew CFVL, gear registration, fisherman's licence and a fishing logsheet under FAO 198-1 s.2018, with an MARINA safety certificate and a VMS requirement. The Supreme Court struck down the VMS/e-catch order FAO 266 (decision 21 Jan 2026, published 3 Aug 2026), and BFAR filed a motion for reconsideration on 14 Aug 2026, so status is in flux. Buyers are mostly individual fishers who will not pay. Candidates C2 and C3.

coverage.category: 33. Micro-business tax and invoicing duties: sari-sari stores, EOPT RA 11976, BMBE, e-invoicing for micro sellers
coverage.found: The EOPT Act removed the PHP 500 annual registration fee (BIR stopped collecting from 22 Jan 2024; one 2025 guide still lists it, so the sources conflict). Books of accounts are registered through ORUS. Non-VAT stores with sales of PHP 3M or less file quarterly percentage tax on 2551Q, or elect the 8% option. BIR's 31 Dec 2026 e-invoicing date (RMC 098-2026, 22 Sep 2026) exempts micro taxpayers and reaches e-commerce sellers and users of computerised accounting systems. BMBE (RA 9178) is an income-tax exemption requiring a DTI certificate. A micro-store quarterly filing tool is generic bookkeeping and tax software, and the known payroll, 2307 and e-commerce ideas are already rejected. Candidate C4 (weak).

coverage.category: 34. Agricultural and food-safety licensing for small food sellers: NMIS meat dealers and cold storage, BPI SPSIC
coverage.found: NMIS licence to operate (LTO) is annual (RA 9296), renewed within 60 days before expiry through the NARIS portal or the regional office. The covered establishments are slaughterhouses, poultry dressing plants, cutting plants, cold storage warehouses and meat distribution centres; retail meat shops are not clearly covered and are handled by LGU meat inspectors (unverified). Cold storage renewal needs a DENR-EMB permit, a sanitary permit, a temperature data logger and a 2-year client list. NMIS proposed interim guidelines in Dec 2025 (6-month initial licence, 1-year renewal, 3-year combined renewal and GMP); whether adopted is unknown. BPI importer registration lasts 3 years. Each shipment needs an SPSIC, which must be used within 20 days for fresh produce, and the DA Trade System enrolment is mandatory. Customs brokers and consultants probably already do this (unverified). Candidates C5 and C6.

coverage.category: 35. Barangay and local registers kept by small operators: BFP FSIC, sanitary permit, health certificates, barangay clearance, Mayor's permit conditions
coverage.found: The FSIC (RA 9514) is annual and a prerequisite for Mayor's permit renewal. The BFP has an online Fire Safety Inspection System (FSIS). ARTA kept fee processes unchanged 1 Jan-30 Jun 2026 and proposed integrating FSIS with LGU eBOSS. Many LGUs (Antipolo from 5 Jan 2026, Valencia) run full eBOSS with online payment, which erodes the paperwork pain. The sanitary permit is per site from the City or Municipal Health Office (PD 856). Renewal typically needs a monthly microbiological water test from a DOH-accredited lab, a monthly pest control report, a yearly physico-chemical test, and per-employee health certificates (chest X-ray valid 1 year, urinalysis, fecalysis valid about 1 month, per LGU). Consultants such as Triple i sell liaison services. No reminder or tracker app found. Candidate C7. A multi-branch BPLO tracker was already covered by the first pass.

coverage.category: 36. Mining and quarry small operators: Minahang Bayan, ISAG/quarry permits, BSP gold buyers (RA 11256)
coverage.found: Sand-and-gravel and quarry permits of 5 ha or less are issued by the provincial governor through the Provincial Mining Regulatory Board (RA 7942, RA 7160). Permit types are ISAG, CSAG, pebble picking, quarry and gratuitous permits. MGB Form 08-4 requires quarterly production reports within 10 days after each quarter, to the governor, with copies to the MGB Regional Director and the municipal treasurer. Governors may inspect books, buyers and selling prices, and local sand-and-gravel fee ordinances apply. Small-scale mining is allowed only in a declared Minahang Bayan (53 declared as of July 2025). Registered miners and accredited traders get tax exemption on gold sold to the BSP under RA 11256 (RR 4-2020); BSP accreditation and certification are required, with a 3-year transition from 2020 that may be extended. Miners report slow and costly BSP selling, and Cebuana Lhuillier is an accredited buyer. The MGB small-scale mining production report format was not found. Candidates C8 and C9.

result.competitor: I found no Philippine product that handles DHSUD re-registration or annual-report preparation. Qmunidad, a Philippine village-management platform at PHP 999/month per village, covers guards, visitors and dues; I saw no compliance features (Product Hunt listing only). Foreign generic HOA tools (HOA Buddy, HOA Hub, Perfect HOA, Enumerate) are not localized for DHSUD. Developer-run condo dues payment links (DMCI with PayMongo) are not relevant. I found no DHSUD online portal for filing; DHSUD publishes only a status list of HOAs. Tagalog-language queries were not run.
result.duty: RA 9904 Sec 4 plus revised IRR (2024) Sec 32 require subdivision and government-housing HOAs previously registered with SEC/HIGC to re-register with DHSUD. DHSUD Department Order 2026-007 (Sec. Aliling) extends the deadline from 18 Jun 2026 to 18 Dec 2026. HOAs registered under HLURB and condo corporations are excluded. Penalty for missing it: automatic suspension, loss of RA 9904 rights, no DHSUD assistance and no HSAC complaints. Re-registration documents, per Respicio commentary: notarized GIS, proof of prior registration, articles, by-laws amended to fit RA 9904, board resolution, officer list, certified member masterlist, code of ethics, proof of area, and fees. Filing is in person at the DHSUD regional office; I found no online channel. Recurring duty: an annual GIS (reportedly due within 120 days after fiscal year-end) and audited or certified financial statements filed with the DHSUD regional office. The PHP 1,000/year late penalty and the audit thresholds come only from commentary, and the commentaries conflict on the thresholds (PHP 600k vs 100k). I have not checked these against a DHSUD circular.
result.market: DHSUD figures: 25,621 registered HOAs (PIA, June 2022); 24,571 monitored (Tribune, 2023 report); more than 26,000 HOAs and neighborhood associations (GMA, undated). The subset that must re-register (those once registered with SEC/HIGC) is not quantified in any source I found. Most are small volunteer-run subdivision and government-housing associations.
result.reason: The duty is real. DHSUD DO 2026-007 moves the re-registration deadline for HOAs once registered with SEC/HIGC to 18 Dec 2026, and HOAs that miss it are automatically suspended under revised IRR Sec 32. The annual GIS and financial statements add a recurring filing, but its due date and penalty figures come only from commentary. Filing appears to be on paper at DHSUD regional offices; I found no online portal. No local product handles DHSUD documents. Qmunidad covers dues and guards, and the foreign tools are generic. However, buyers are volunteer boards with little budget. The re-registration is a one-off, and the number of SEC/HIGC-era HOAs is unknown. Out of roughly 25,000 registered HOAs, the paying market is small, so a done-for-you service suits this better than SaaS.

result.competitor: No product built for small Philippine money changers was found. Tookitaki sells enterprise AML (screening, monitoring, CTR/STR filing). Verihubs sells eKYC, watchlist screening and OCR APIs aimed at agent networks. Foreign bureau-de-change software exists, such as FXPlus, Money Exchanger Plus and CurrencyXchanger on Capterra, but none shows BSP or AMLC reporting. CTR and STR filing goes through the free AMLC portal (GoTRACS), so a product's value would be logging transactions, KYC records, the AML programme document and preparing the files, not the filing itself. Not checked: Philippine POS vendors for forex counters, and whether 247 RemitPlus is still sold.
result.duty: The duty is real and in force. BSP Circular No. 1206 (23 Dec 2024, Monetary Board Res. 1362) removed MORNBFI Secs 901-N and 902-N and replaced them with the M-Regulations. These cover remittance transfer companies, money changers and FX dealers. A second circular, reported as No. 1222 (MB approval 14 Aug 2025), amends the reporting rules in Secs 151-M to 154-M. Secondary summaries say it sets reporting standards, monetary and non-monetary sanctions, and audited financial statement deadlines. I could not open its full text (HTTP 429). Separately, the AML law (RA 9160, as amended by RA 11211) requires: (1) registration with the AMLC on portal.amlc.gov.ph; (2) covered transaction reports for cash over PHP 500,000 in one banking day, due within 5 working days; (3) suspicious transaction reports with no threshold, due the next working day after suspicion arises, filed through GoTRACS. The CTR and STR terms come from secondary sources only, not checked against AMLC text. Enforcement is real: MB cancelled Prince Rockwell, Kings Hopewell and World Reliance for persistent AMLA violations (CL-2025-028), barred 4 unregistered operators (CL-2025-021), and cancelled sole proprietorships (Edzen, World Wide Money Changer). Not verified: exact BSP report forms, how often they are due, and penalty amounts per day of delay.
result.market: The claim cites 7,357 registered MSBs at end-2023 (secondary source). Verihubs cites BSP data of about 5,300 head offices, 12,700 branches and 6,700 pawnshops holding MSB licences, but its totals do not add up. Likely buyers are a few thousand single-office changers and remittance agents. I did not find an official 2024 or 2025 count.
result.reason: The duty is mandatory and enforced: BSP cancels registrations over AML lapses every year, and the M-Regulations were tightened in 2024-25. I found no affordable tool for small money changers. Several things hold the score down. Small changers rarely handle single cash deals over PHP 500k, so routine CTR filing is light. Filing is done on the free AMLC portal. Many operators are cash-only family businesses that are hard to reach and will pay little. Some BSP reporting forms may already be simple templates. A records, KYC and AML-programme pack plus a checklist of BSP reports is a workable MVP. It could be sold through the money changer associations, but the market is only a few thousand firms and willingness to pay is uncertain.

result.competitor: I found no Philippine-specific notarial register or monthly-report tool for paper notaries. NotarioPH (from the claim) did not appear in my searches, so whether it is live and what it costs remain unverified. IBP eNotary (enotary.ibp.ph) only connects clients with e-notaries. Foreign tools such as NotaryGadget and NotaryAssist are built for the US and do not produce PH clerk-of-court reports. Accredited e-notarization facility providers under A.M. 24-10-14-SC will cover e-notaries, not the monthly report of paper notaries. Notaries can still meet the duty by hand with a scanner and email, which is the main substitute.
result.duty: The 2004 Rules on Notarial Practice (A.M. No. 02-8-13-SC), as amended by the SC en banc resolution of 4 March 2025, require every commissioned notary to email the clerk of court a PDF of the month's notarial entries plus PDF duplicate originals within the first 10 days of the next month. The email must come from the notary's registered professional email, carry the subject "Notary Report of [Name] for [Month Year]", attach files directly (no ZIP, RAR or cloud links), mark batches "Batch x of y" and include a numbered inventory. A nil statement is required if there were no entries. Signatories must get an electronic copy within 5 days. Penalties are non-renewal, temporary disqualification or revocation. Reported implementing issuance: OCA Circular 197-2025. The 2025 date is confirmed by Aureada and Tribune; the official text was not fetched. Local OCC practice varies, e.g. RTC-OCC Iligan's verification schedule and certificate. E-notarization (A.M. 24-10-14-SC, effective 9 Mar 2025) is a separate regime with an Electronic Notarial Book and a central SC database. Reports say it is not yet operating because the Electronic Notary Services body has not been constituted.
result.market: Not found. There is no published national count of commissioned notaries. A 2023 FOI request to the DOJ for this was denied and redirected to the SC. Executive judges send quarterly lists of commissioned notaries to the OCA (OCA Circular 111-2022-A, amended 2024), but these are not published. Commissions are issued per RTC jurisdiction and generally run for 2 years.
result.reason: The duty is real, but it is only confirmed through secondary sources. The SC en banc resolution of 4 Mar 2025 amended the 2004 Rules on Notarial Practice (A.M. 02-8-13-SC). Each month, notaries must email the clerk of court a PDF of the month's entries and each instrument, using a set subject line, direct attachments only (no ZIP or cloud links), batches and an inventory. Penalties include non-renewal and revocation. I found no PH tool for ordinary notaries that produces this report: search did not surface NotarioPH, and IBP eNotary does not do it. Weaknesses: the job is mostly scanning, renaming and emailing, so willingness to pay is likely low. Local clerks of court add their own steps, as Iligan's verification schedule shows. The number of notaries is unknown, and the move to e-notarization (with a central SC database) may make the tool redundant over time.

result.competitor: CDA's own CAIS is a free online system for encoding and submitting the reports, and micro co-ops get free simplified Excel/Canva templates. CDA regional offices run free hands-on CAIS workshops, and field staff help encode reports. The AFS, and in practice the audit reports, come from CDA-accredited external auditors (CEAs), which is the same objection that killed K17. Co-op core and accounting systems: CoopVault (WeSupport Inc.) claims it is "100% CDA & BSP compliant" and tracks CDA, BSP, CIC and BIR filings, and iAccs (coreDev) offers regulatory agency reports. I found no product dedicated to preparing the CAPR or CAIS pack, and no published rates for consultants.
result.duty: Confirmed. CDA MC 2025-02 (based on RA 9520 Art. 53) applies to all co-ops except CSF co-ops. The yearly CAPR pack is due within 120 days of year end (30 Apr 2026 for FY2025, moved to 31 May 2026 by MC 2026-07). The pack covers the AFS from a CDA-accredited CEA, SAR, PAR (GMAR, STEPS, summary audit), the semi-annual mediation/conciliation report, LOTA and a sworn statement, plus ATIR/ABR for co-ops holding a CTE. Penalties: P100 per day of delay for small, medium and large co-ops, no COC, possible revocation of the COR, and possible revocation of the BIR CTE if ATIR/ABR is missing. Micro co-ops (assets under P3M) are excepted from the fine and file simplified reports through the CDA Online Services tab or by email using CDA templates. I could not confirm whether they are fully exempt from the report list. The MC 2025-02 PDF did not render as text, so I relied on CDA regional advisories.
result.market: CDA 2021 statistics (FY2020 data): 20,467 co-ops, of which 13,257 are micro, 3,961 small, 2,438 medium and 811 large. That leaves about 7,200 non-micro co-ops carrying the full pack and fine. A PNA piece says there were over 20,105 co-ops in 2022. I found no 2025 figure.
result.reason: The duty is real and in force. CDA MC 2025-02 requires every co-op except CSF co-ops to file a CAPR within 120 days of year end, with an AFS from a CDA-accredited external auditor (CEA), SAR, PAR/STEPS, a mediation report, LOTA and a sworn statement. Late filing costs P100 a day for small, medium and large co-ops, and the penalties also include losing the COC and revocation. Filing goes through the free CAIS portal, and micro co-ops use simplified templates from CDA. The hardest parts (AFS, and the audit reports PAR/SAR) are tied to CEAs, which is the K17 objection. Core systems such as CoopVault and iAccs claim CDA/regulatory reporting. I found no standalone CAPR or CAIS-prep tool. The remaining encoding work is light, and CDA field staff help with it for free.

result.competitor: I found no Philippine product or provincial online portal for permittee production reports. Systems are paper-based: provinces print delivery-receipt booklets (Camarines Norte RFQ for 1,700 stubs), Occidental Mindoro and Davao run checkpoints, and Pampanga inventories receipt booklets. Foreign quarry ERPs (Proginov, France) do weighbridge and delivery-note work but nothing PH-specific. I did not run a Filipino-language search.
result.duty: Under RA 7942 (Mining Act) and its implementing rules, plus RA 7160 sec. 138 (provincial sand and gravel tax), MGB Form 08-4 commercial sand and gravel permits (and 08-4A/08-4B) require a quarterly production report within 10 days after quarter end. It goes to the Provincial Governor or City Mayor, with copies to the MGB Regional Director and the municipal treasurers. It covers the volume extracted, removed or disposed and the fees paid. A final report is due at the end of the permit term. Some provincial permits instead require monthly reports to the treasurer and governor (Cebu 2013, Negros Oriental). Penalties: permit suspension or cancellation, plus provincial tax surcharges (Bataan: 10% tax and a surcharge if extraction came before payment). The templates are old .doc files, and I did not verify the current form version.
result.market: I found no national register. Partial counts: Antique has 94 permittees; MGB-7 2022 Table 7 shows LGU-issued commercial sand and gravel permits per Central Visayas province of about 1 to 124 (PDF returned 403, so this is from the snippet); Albay had 106 operators reviewed; Surigao del Sur cancelled 103 permits (2010). A rough national estimate is low thousands of LGU permittees (unverified).
result.reason: The duty is real. The MGB permit templates (Form 08-4, and 08-4B for exclusive, government and private gratuitous permits) require a production report within 10 days after each quarter to the Governor or City Mayor, with copies to MGB and the treasurers. Some provinces require it monthly (Cebu, Negros Oriental). I found no Philippine software or provincial e-filing that does the job. Control is paper-based: delivery-receipt booklets issued by the province, checkpoints, and treasurer collection. But the report itself is short and simple, so the pain is low. Provinces own the real control point, the delivery receipts and the tax per load. Operators are few (about 20 to 125 per province, perhaps a few thousand nationally, not verified), often politically connected, and unlikely to pay. Selling to provinces instead would be building the state's system, which is out of scope.

result.competitor: No FPA-specific dealer compliance software found. Generic dealer and inventory tools such as BeatRoute exist.
result.duty: FPA dealer licence (PD 1144), renewed about yearly with inspection. Periodic reporting not confirmed. Online-selling revocation under MC 1 s.2026.
result.market: Not found. No dealer count located.
result.reason: Licensing duty is real (PD 1144; dealers need an FPA licence, about one year per an older government listing; Accredited Safety Dispenser required; FPA inspection at renewal; day-to-day purchase/sale/use books expected). FPA MC No.1 s.2026 targets online sellers, not dealer paperwork. I found no formal periodic dealer sales or stock report, and no renewal checklist. The traceability rule is only proposed in the FY2026 Annual Regulatory Plan. I found no niche competitor, but generic dealer and inventory apps exist, such as BeatRoute. Dealers are many but small and fragmented, with an annual rather than frequent duty, so the pain is low. The market count was not found.

The duty is real: DMW licensing carries an escrow deposit, annual surety bond, and audited financial statements at renewal. SunStar reports escrow raised to PHP 1.5M and regular licence validity extended to 6 years. I found no official DMW issuance confirming this, and secondary sources conflict on escrow (1M vs 2M). Reporting frequency and channel were not found. Agencies number about 3,700 (undated secondary figure). I found no DMW-specific compliance software, but only generic recruitment tools with 'compliance tracking'. Licences last 4-6 years, so renewal is infrequent. Audited FS and escrow are handled by auditors and banks, not software. DMW uses its own portals for contract processing. Small, niche market with low frequency, so the score is low.

The NWRB Economic Regulatory Framework (Res. 25-0818, adopted 2019) is real and sorts utilities into three categories, including community-based ones. It requires CPC applicants to follow the tariff methodology, and tariff review comes every 5 years or as necessary. I found no recurring annual-report duty with a stated penalty for BAWASA/RWSA. The "1,700" count is unconfirmed; a Senate document says about 2,200 small utilities exist. Competition was not checked well. I found only one academic custom billing tool for a waterworks association (eBillH20, BOWASA) and no commercial vendor. Buyers are volunteer-run, pay little, and file rarely, so recurrence is weak. I ran 2 searches and no fetches.

Duty is real: LTO accredits driving schools via the CAC-DSMC. MC VDM-2023-2460 sets course standards. The 8-hour practical course is mandatory, and 12 NCR schools were suspended in March 2026 and revoked in April 2026. Schools must transmit results and certificates electronically through the LTO's LTMS portal. That portal is a state system, so the reporting job is largely handled by the state tool. The market looks small, with a few hundred schools in a 2021 list. I did not find the current count, a frequency or penalty schedule, or any third-party software, so the competition check is incomplete. Likely low willingness to pay and a dependence on LTMS access. Not refuted, but weak.

Halal certification in the Philippines is voluntary. The Grab Davao pilot (MoU 9 Sep 2026) requires NCMF endorsement only for the halal tag on GrabFood, which is a platform condition, not a legal duty. I found no statutory recurring filing. Only a private certifier (HDI) states a 1-year renewable validity, so that is certifier policy. Accreditation authority is disputed between NCMF and DTI-PAB. Davao has a city ordinance requiring certification from an NCMF-accredited body for halal-labelled food, but this is local and narrow. I did not search for competing software. I found no merchant count. The buyer pool is small, willingness to pay is low, and the NCMF endorsement process is unclear. This fails the mandatory-duty test.

The duty is real under RA 10361. Employers must keep a barangay registry entry and a written contract. They must register the worker with SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG, remit monthly, and file a separation report within 30 days. Violations carry fines of PHP 10,000 to 40,000, and unpaid SSS contributions add 2% a month. I found no dedicated household-employer app. SweldoPH is only a free calculator and guide. Agencies offer free unified forms and online portals (My.SSS, Virtual Pag-IBIG). An old BayadLoad e-money route exists. Weak points: a consumer buyer, low enforcement, low willingness to pay, and no B2B channel. I did not find a household count (not reached). The idea is unproven and weak.

Duty is real: PD 1612 (Anti-Fencing Law) and its rules require station-commander clearance for secondhand articles, plus affidavits and inventories of acquisitions with supplier names and addresses. Local ordinances add permits. I found no junkshop-specific software in two searches, but I did not look for generic POS or inventory tools. Weak points: no national digital filing, so police would have to accept a printout. Enforcement looks uneven and sometimes informal (Valenzuela "kotong" case). Shops are mostly unregistered micro-enterprises. Quezon City has about 680 registered shops. No national count was found. Digital readiness and willingness to pay are low, and distribution would be LGU-by-LGU. The Naga ordinance PDF was unreadable, so its inspection terms are unverified.

result.duty: Monthly LTO report applies to vehicle importers, distributors and dealers (Sec. 10) and to manufacturers of engine blocks, chassis or bodies (Sec. 11). It does not clearly apply to used-parts dealers or dismantlers. No Sec. 10/11 penalty was seen in the fetched text.
result.market: Not quantified; no register of used-parts dealers or dismantlers found.
result.reason: RA 10883 Sec. 10 (lawyerly.ph text) obliges only those importing, distributing, buying and selling motor vehicles to keep stock records and report monthly to LTO. Sec. 11 covers manufacturers of engine blocks, chassis or bodies. Used-parts dealers and dismantlers are not named, and the Act does not use the word "dismantler". Sec. 17 only bans trading parts from carnapped vehicles. The "20 days" sales rule was not found in the text. LTO AO AVT-2014-023 covers accreditation and stock reporting for MAIRDOEs (vehicle and component importers, dealers), and I could not confirm it reaches parts sellers. Duty on this buyer group is unproven, so it is a niche, fragmented, informal market. No competitor search was run. LTMS channel not checked.

DOT accreditation of hotels, pension houses, tourist inns and homestays is established under the Progressive Accreditation System (MC 2018-03). The Mabuhay Accommodation tiers are an old regime. No source found shows that accreditation is mandatory for Airbnb-type hosts, or gives a renewal cycle or penalty. The June 2026 Freeman item mentions only an unnamed national directive. The Hotel Code 1987 register duty was not confirmed as applying to rentals. Competition is partial: Hotelogix, Xenia and Optima PMS exist, but no register-specific tool was checked. No register of host numbers was found. Hosts are fragmented, the duty is unclear, and the product would be a thin PMS-like tool, hence a low score. Not checked: LGU tourism taxes and the directive text.
